content.value_statement: Polymarket integrations require many APIs, authentication flows, and streaming topics. This skill organizes the reference material so agents can plan market data, trading, and WebSocket workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains Polymarket market, event, tag, price, order book, and comment API references.
Guides WebSocket subscriptions for activity, comments, RFQ, crypto prices, and CLOB market updates.
Summarizes authentication concepts for public data, user data, and CLOB trading operations.
Helps choose filters, topics, and endpoints for market monitoring applications.
Provides examples for TypeScript and Python client usage from included reference documents.
Covers trading concepts such as orders, balances, allowances, price changes, and settlement.
limitations: It does not place trades or connect to Polymarket by itself.
It does not verify current regulations, user eligibility, or financial suitability.
It depends on the included documentation and may lag behind Polymarket platform changes.
It cannot protect private keys or API secrets shared directly in a prompt.

use_cases.title: Market Data Dashboard
use_cases.description: Identify the API endpoints and fields needed to display events, markets, prices, and order book data.

use_cases.title: Live Trade Monitor
use_cases.description: Design subscriptions for real-time trades, price changes, comments, and crypto price updates.

use_cases.title: Trading Client Integration
use_cases.description: Plan authentication, order placement, balance checks, and error handling for a CLOB client workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Find Market Data Endpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Polymarket skill to list the endpoints I need for events, markets, prices, and tags. Explain when to use each endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Plan WebSocket Subscriptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Polymarket skill to design WebSocket subscriptions for a live market monitor. Include topics, message types, filters, and reconnect concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review Trading Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Polymarket skill to outline a safe CLOB trading flow from credentials to order placement. Include checks before submitting an order.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementation Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Polymarket skill to compare REST polling, WebSocket streaming, and client libraries for my use case. Recommend a design with operational risks.

output_examples.input: I need a dashboard for active crypto prediction markets.
output: Recommended endpoints for market discovery, tag filtering, prices, and order books.
A data refresh plan that separates slow market metadata from fast price data.
Notes about rate limits, closed markets, and user-facing latency expectations.

output_examples.input: I want to track live comments and trades for one event.
output: A subscription plan for activity and comments topics with event or market filters.
Message handling guidance for reconnects, duplicate events, and high-volume streams.
A short checklist for authentication only when private user streams are required.

output_examples.input: Review my Polymarket trading integration plan.
output: A step-by-step review of credentials, balance checks, allowances, order construction, and error handling.
Warnings about private key handling, test environments, and order confirmation before submission.

best_practices: Use read-only public endpoints until authenticated user data or trading is required.
Keep private keys and API secrets outside prompts, logs, source control, and shared transcripts.
Apply narrow WebSocket filters and handle reconnects, rate limits, and duplicate messages.
anti_patterns: Do not paste wallet private keys, API secrets, or passphrases into an AI chat.
Do not submit trades from generated code without independent review and explicit confirmation.
Do not subscribe to wildcard streams in production without backpressure and monitoring.

faq.question: Can this skill trade on Polymarket for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and reference material. Users must control credentials, code execution, and trade confirmation.

faq.question: Does it support real-time data?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents WebSocket topics for trades, comments, RFQ events, crypto prices, and CLOB market data.

faq.question: Does it require private keys?
faq.answer: Public market data does not require private keys. Authenticated trading and private user streams require user-managed credentials.

faq.question: Is the documentation current?
faq.answer: The skill uses bundled reference files. Verify important endpoint behavior against current Polymarket documentation before production use.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The included examples focus on TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python clients.

faq.question: What should I check before production use?
faq.answer: Review authentication, rate limits, reconnect logic, order validation, secret storage, and legal requirements for your jurisdiction.
